issues.description: Tab-only mode still intercepts non-Tab navigation keys and forwards them to the editor, breaking arrow/PageUp/Escape behavior in the popup.
issues.detail: The early-return branch fires for ANY key that isn't Tab (including Up/Down/PageUp/PageDown/Escape/Home/End). It hides the popup and replays the event to the textedit, so the user can no longer navigate the completion list with arrow keys when 'use_enter_for_completions' is False. The guard should only trigger for Enter/Return.

issues.description: Calling self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event) directly bypasses Qt's event dispatch and may re-enter completion logic.
issues.detail: Directly invoking keyPressEvent on the textedit can skip event filters, shortcut handling, and IME composition. A safer pattern used elsewhere in Spyder is QApplication.sendEvent or letting hide() take effect and re-posting the event. This risks subtle re-entrancy where hiding the popup triggers another completion request mid-keypress.

issues.description: No migration/default handling for existing user configs missing 'use_enter_for_completions'.
issues.detail: The default is added to spyder/config/main.py but CONF_VERSION does not appear to be bumped in the diff. Existing users on older config versions may hit a KeyError from get_conf, or the new default may not propagate. Verify the conf system falls back to the new default rather than raising.

issues.description: PEP 8 style: 'not key == Qt.Key_Tab' should be 'key != Qt.Key_Tab'.
issues.detail: Minor readability nit. The double-negation form is harder to scan and violates standard Python style guidance. Also, Tab is not the only accept key historically — some users use Shift+Tab or have backtab — though that is a separate scope concern.

issues.description: No tests added for the new completion-accept behavior.
issues.detail: This changes a keyboard-handling code path that users rely on heavily. A small unit test toggling the conf option and asserting that Enter does/does not accept a completion would catch regressions, especially given how easy it is to break arrow-key navigation as flagged above.

issues.description: get_conf called on every keypress while popup is visible — minor inefficiency and tight coupling.
issues.detail: Reading the conf inside keyPressEvent on every key adds an unnecessary lookup per keystroke. Caching the value on popup show, or subscribing to conf changes, would be cleaner and matches patterns used elsewhere in the editor widget.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful option to disable Enter for accepting completions, but the implementation in completion.py has a significant logic bug: the early-return branch fires for any non-Tab key, which would break arrow-key navigation, Escape handling, and other expected popup behavior when the option is disabled. The condition should specifically check for Enter/Return rather than 'not Tab'. Secondary concerns include calling keyPressEvent directly on the textedit (bypassing event dispatch), missing conf-migration handling, and lack of tests for the new behavior. The UI/config additions themselves look correct.
